**The force push was blocked by a policy guard and did not happen.** The remote is unchanged — `origin/main` is still at `aadc28d`.

The command I intended to run, and which needs a person to carry out:

```
git push --force-with-lease=main:aadc28dc2e4b7496fa82f15eda2e93c1cf99109c origin main
```

The `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha>` form was to make the push abort if the remote had moved past `aadc28d` since my fetch. The guard rejected it anyway: `main` is protected, and force-push there can permanently lose remote commits. It told me not to retry or route around it, so I haven't.

**What I did do:** tagged the remote-only commit locally so it's recoverable —

```
backup/origin-main-before-force-push -> aadc28d
```

That tag is local only; it hasn't been pushed, so it dies with this checkout.

| yours | `5575b25` fold: merge the reversal fix | `// local work` |

If it isn't meant to go, the cleanest fix needs no force push at all:

